Permanent text highlighting — design

Date: 2026-08-22 Status: Draft, pending approval

A signed-in reader selects text on a manual page at /manual-del-color-vivo/{section}, a floating pill reading subrayar appears, and clicking it persists the highlight. The highlight is repainted every time that reader returns to the section.

Deferred out of this version and documented separately in docs/highlight-next-nice-to-haves.md: a highlight-count marker in the table of contents, and a “mis subrayados” index page.

Decisions

| Question | Decision | | — | — | | Visibility | Private to the reader who made it | | Removal | Click an existing highlight → pill reads “quitar subrayado” | | Highlightable surface | The article body only | | Pill actions | “subrayar” only — no copy, no comment | | Mobile placement | Pill below the selection, clearing the native iOS/Android menu | | Overlaps | Merge into one highlight | | Multi-block selections | One row per block element | | Colour | A new manual-theme token, not the browser’s selection blue | | Orphaned highlights | Silently skipped at render, row kept | | Save feedback | Optimistic, reverted on failure | | Selection rules | Trim whitespace, minimum length, links allowed, maximum length | | Dismissal | Clearing the selection, scrolling, or Escape | | Accessibility | Pill is a real focusable button; keyboard selection works end to end | | Anchoring | Block hash + verified offsets | | Painting | CSS Custom Highlight API; pill hidden where unsupported | | Delivery | Inline prop on manual#show | | Merging | Client unions, server validates | | JS tests | Vitest, scoped to the anchoring library |

1. Data model

highlights
  id
  user_id       bigint  not null, fk
  section_path  string  not null      # "el-origen-del-color/pigmentos"
  group_key     uuid    not null      # links rows created by one selection
  block_hash    string  not null      # FNV-1a of the block's normalized text
  block_index   integer not null      # ordinal of the block within the article
  start_offset  integer not null      # into the block's *normalized* text
  end_offset    integer not null
  text          text    not null
  timestamps

index [user_id, section_path]         # the read path
index [user_id, group_key]            # removal
check  start_offset >= 0 AND end_offset > start_offset

section_path is a string key, not a foreign key, because manual sections are not database rows — they come from the hardcoded Manual::TABLE_OF_CONTENTS tree in app/models/manual.rb. This follows Comment and ManualVisit.

block_index is consulted only when block_hash matches more than one block, so it never causes the positional drift that pure ordinal anchoring would.

Highlight validates section_path through Manual.path?(section_path.split("/")), reusing Comment#section_path_must_exist, and caps text at 5000 characters at both the validation and column level.

User gains has_many :highlights, dependent: :destroy.

2. Anchoring algorithm

Lives in app/frontend/lib/highlights/anchor.js as pure functions, which is what makes it testable under Vitest.

Normalization

A block is a leaf block element: p, li, h2, h3, blockquote, dd — the innermost element that contains text and no nested block. A recipe with eight steps has eight independent anchors, so editing step three orphans only step three.

For each block, normalizedText is its textContent with runs of whitespace collapsed to a single space, then trimmed. A single TreeWalker pass produces both that string and an index map from each normalized character position back to a (textNode, offset) pair.

Every offset in the schema indexes this normalized string, never raw textContent.

Hashing

FNV-1a 32-bit over normalizedText, rendered as hex. Chosen over SHA-256 because crypto.subtle is asynchronous; collisions across the ~10 blocks of a section are negligible, and block_index breaks ties.

This algorithm is frozen once shipped. Changing it orphans every existing row.

Capture

  1. Reject if either endpoint of the selection falls outside the content wrapper.
  2. Trim whitespace inward from both edges.
  3. Enumerate the leaf blocks the range intersects.
  4. Per block, map the DOM sub-range through the index map into normalized offsets.
  5. Reject selections under 3 or over 5000 characters.

Resolution

Per stored row:

  1. Find candidate blocks by block_hash; disambiguate with block_index.
  2. Slice [start_offset, end_offset) out of the block’s normalized text.
  3. Verify the slice equals the stored text.
  4. On mismatch, fall back to indexOf(text) within that block.
  5. If still not found, skip silently and keep the row.

Step 3 is what guarantees that a stale anchor never paints the wrong words — the failure mode is an invisible highlight, never a misplaced one.

3. Painting

One registry entry holds every range:

CSS.highlights.set('subrayado', new Highlight(...ranges))

@theme manual-theme {
  --color-manual-highlight: /* warm tint derived from --color-manual-orange */;
}
::highlight(subrayado) { background-color: var(--color-manual-highlight); }

::selection uses the same token, so the live selection and the persisted highlight are visually identical.

Browser support

Feature gate on 'highlights' in CSS. Where absent, the pill is hidden entirely, so no reader can create a highlight they will never see.

| Browser | Shipped | Age at 2026-08 | | — | — | — | | Chrome / Edge 105 | Sept 2022 | ~4 years | | Safari 17.2 | Dec 2023 | ~2 yr 8 mo | | Firefox 140 | June 2025 | ~14 months |

Baseline “newly available” since June 2025. The excluded population is essentially iPhones that cannot run iOS 17.2 — 2017 and earlier — since every iOS browser uses Safari’s engine. Android is effectively unaffected: Chrome updates through the Play Store independently of the OS version.

Hit-testing for removal

caretPositionFromPoint(), falling back to caretRangeFromPoint() on WebKit, turns a click into a block plus a normalized offset, which is then matched against the loaded rows. More reliable than intersecting Range.getClientRects().

Re-render safety

This is the one real hazard. Range objects point at live DOM nodes, and the <article> subtree is React-owned.

Delivery is inline, so the highlights prop is stable — but the deferred comments prop still re-renders the page after first paint. The resolver therefore re-runs in a useEffect keyed on [section, highlights, comments]. Re-resolution costs a few milliseconds.

The CSS Custom Highlight API was chosen over <mark> DOM wrapping precisely because it mutates nothing: a React re-render can invalidate ranges, but it cannot silently destroy markup we injected.

SSR

All of the above runs inside useEffect, with no browser globals at module scope, so the Vite/Inertia SSR path in app/frontend/ssr/ssr.jsx is unaffected.

4. Interaction

Selecting text inside <article> shows the pill anchored below range.getBoundingClientRect().bottom — below, not above, so it clears the native iOS/Android selection menu. It is a real focusable <button>, so keyboard selection with Shift+arrows works end to end. It is dismissed by collapsing the selection, by scrolling, or by Escape.

Clicking an existing highlight shows the same pill reading quitar subrayado, which removes the entire group_key — so a three-paragraph highlight disappears as one thing.

Saving is optimistic: the tint appears immediately and the request fires behind it. On failure the previous ranges are restored and a transient Spanish message is shown.

5. Merge semantics

Before posting, the client:

  1. Finds existing rows in the affected blocks whose ranges overlap or touch the new selection.
  2. Expands to those rows’ full groups — a merge that touches one block of a three-block group absorbs all three.
  3. Unions the ranges per block.
  4. Posts the union, replacing every affected row with a fresh group_key.

The invariant this preserves: what the reader sees as one continuous highlight is always exactly one group, so “quitar” always removes exactly that.

POST /highlights
{
  section_path,
  blocks: [{ block_hash, block_index, start_offset, end_offset, text }],
  replaces: [id, ...]
}

The server validates, then performs one transaction — delete the replaced rows, insert the new ones under a fresh group_key:

  • section_path resolves through Manual.path?
  • end_offset > start_offset >= 0
  • text.length == end_offset - start_offset — a cheap consistency check that catches most client-side offset bugs
  • every replaces id belongs to Current.user and to this section_path
  • every replaced row genuinely overlaps a submitted block with the same block_hash and block_index

Rails 8’s controller-level rate_limit guards the action, as Users::SessionsController already does.

DELETE /highlights/:id destroys the row’s whole group, scoped to Current.user.

6. Delivery

ManualController#show adds an inline highlights prop — a single query on [user_id, section_path], no serializer needed beyond a select. Inline rather than InertiaRails.defer so highlights paint on first render, with no flash of unhighlighted text.

Plate pages (node[:plate]) receive neither the prop nor the component, the same way they already receive no comment thread.

7. Files

| File | Change | | — | — | | db/migrate/*_create_highlights.rb | new | | app/models/highlight.rb | new | | app/models/user.rb | has_many :highlights | | app/controllers/highlights_controller.rb | new | | app/controllers/manual_controller.rb | highlights prop on #show | | config/routes.rb | resources :highlights, only: [:create, :destroy] | | app/frontend/lib/highlights/anchor.js | new — pure anchoring functions | | app/frontend/components/manual/Highlighter.jsx | new — capture, pill, painting | | app/frontend/components/ManualLayout.jsx | mount Highlighter around the article | | app/frontend/entrypoints/application.css | token, ::highlight, ::selection | | package.json, vitest.config.ts | new dev dependency, jsdom environment |

8. Testing

RSpec request specs — create; multi-block create; merge-and-replace; forged section_path; another user’s ids in replaces; non-overlapping replaces rejected; group destroy; destroy scoped to owner; rate limit.

Model spec — validations and the check constraint.

Vitest, scoped to app/frontend/lib/highlights/ — normalization, the index map, hash stability, offset resolution, verify-and-fallback, orphan skip, merge unioning. This logic is genuinely unreachable from RSpec, which is the whole justification for adding a JS test runner to a repo that has none.

Manual browser verification — pill placement on desktop and mobile, Escape dismissal, and repaint after the deferred comments prop arrives.

9. Judgment calls and risks

No per-section highlight cap. Declined during design, but delivery is inline on every manual page load, so the prop is unbounded. A pathological reader could bloat their own page loads. Blast radius is one user, so this is acceptable — but it is a self-inflicted risk on the read path, and the cap remains the obvious mitigation if it ever bites.

block_index is the ordinal among leaf blocks article-wide, not per-parent, since it serves only as a tiebreak.

Server-side orphan detection is impossible. Page text lives in JSX shipped in the build, not in the database, so the server can never know whether a row still matches anything. “Silently skip” is necessarily a client-side decision, and any future server-side count of a reader’s highlights will overstate. This is the shared blocker for both deferred features.

The hash algorithm is a frozen interface. Any change to FNV-1a, to the normalization rules, or to the definition of a leaf block orphans every existing highlight.
